native_warning.evidence: Both R67 archives show the same Key_Carrier floating-regions notice that every slice since R58 has had, including the approved R63 and R66 pairs. Each archive has its own layers.json. In both, completely_unsupported_starts is [] for all 13 parts and native_support_moves is 0. Each verify.log shows blocked [] and unsupported_starts {}, and both receipts exited 0 (758 and 864 samples). Each archive has the same six one-anchored runs as R66, at the same stations: layer 10 (1.049 mm); layer 11 (1.02 against R66's 1.015, and 2.158); layer 49 (4.626 mm, G-code line 131309); and layer 155 (3.666 and 6.346). The layer-49 run is the accepted outboard lip-start watch point at assembly X -18.98 to -23.60, Z ~3.04, Y ~33.9. None of the six is in a changed region. The diagonal-corner layers 0-18 have no run to review, and neither does the left saddle zone. The only run the geometry change introduces is a two-anchored 1.41 mm bridge at layer 164: assembly X ~10.6-11.0, Z ~7.15-7.93, Y ~10.85. It sits inside the design66 WINDOW and the 7.25-7.97 lead-in band, so it is the roof of the lead-in at the opening's upper print end. Other run differences from R66 are at unchanged geometry and are all two-anchored: one fewer at layer 59, shorter runs at layer 74, +0.25 mm at layer 156, the layer-160 run gone, and changes at layers 161, 162 and 195. Layer 195 (Y ~4.7) is outside WINDOW. I treat these as toolpath variation. The slicer does not say where its notice comes from. It is accepted as the known notice, not as a reason for supports.

observations: Freeze and provenance. Rehashed at the end of the review: carrier a83ac4df, both archives, audit67 bbc7ab47, checks67 74b9b8e9, design67 86068d97, guide67 52b4c1fd, kit67 9a80dbef, op1-route cf607c69 and assembly-guide c423a07c. design67.py was edited at 16:11 (1dfe5c59 -> 86068d97). That was after the 16:01 STL export, both 16:03 slices, the receipts and the click report, and the STL was not regenerated. The visible change is a docstring correction: the lead-in now 'stops 1.43 mm below the board seat', which matches lead_in.board_seat_z 9.4 minus top 7.97. Equivalence rests on subtraction.json. It was recomputed at 16:12 from the edited source against the unchanged STL: same removals and max section difference 0.000735 mm2. Both archives' pin-fit sources also bind a83ac4df. final/source-checks.log still cites 1dfe5c59 and is stale. Action for the parent: regenerate the carrier from the current source, confirm it reproduces a83ac4df, and refresh that log.

Locality (subtraction.json). The removals are 9.01143 + 67.68125 + 1.42721 = 78.1194 mm3, equal to the volume difference. Pairwise cutter overlaps are 0. Across 313 sections the max difference from R66-minus-cutters is 0.000735 mm2. The carrier is one component. 336 key poses show 0 obstructions, and the backer sweeps are 0.

Battery corner (battery.json diagonal_corner). The diagonal runs from (-24.55, 40.0) to (-22.6, 43.65), 28.1 degrees from print vertical. The outboard edge is unchanged at y38-40 and is -22.637 at y43.6. Unchanged: root_post_front_to_y40 (15.3719), pouch_side_of_post (10.1771) and spring_leaf_and_shoe_unchanged_xor (0). Identical to R66: shoe preload 2.558, retention inboard 7.83 / outboard 4.45, and pack seated/slide overlap 0. In fit.json, battery_seated, battery_slides_in_from_the_rear, side_leaf_can_flex and leaf_is_free_of_floor are unobstructed in both archives. The root post went from 46.589 to 41.687 mm3 and joined_to_deck from 11.15 to 10.009 mm2 (-10%, ungated). By my hand estimate, the bed end of the post is now about 1.0-1.3 mm wide between the diagonal and the pouch face, widening to about 3 mm at Y 40. r67-battery.png against v-below.png shows the requested taper in plan.

Base and moved ties. battery-base.json passes in both archives. The thresholds are unchanged from audit66 (root regions > 0.4 mm2, free lips < 0.05 mm2), and the windows follow the tie stations. Contacts: spring_root_below 2.96 (R66 3.68), root_above 3.56 (3.14), free lips 0. In fin-design.json, the -y fin at X -22.4, Z 3.16 has rooted volume 1.93 mm3 (R66: 2.41 at -22.68). The +y fin at X -22.0, Z 8.47 has 2.66 (R66: 2.46 at -23.8). Total fin section stays 25.5 and fins_on_hinge 0. By hand, the outboard ~0.6 mm of the -y fin is beyond the diagonal at the bed layer and stands on the base sheet, so 'moved onto retained plastic' is mostly but not entirely true. wide-bases.json gives the carrier a connected first layer of 3396.79 mm2 (R66 3401.44), second layer on that base 3389.76, bed edge 2.53. joint.json all_base_contacts is 21.03 (R66 21.37).

Saddle stubs. saddle.json identifies them as R60 leftovers: 67.68 mm3 at X -10.81 to -3.85, touching only the saddle face. independent-guard.json shows 0 overlap and 1.0 mm gaps to both the upper guard and the lower returns, so the stubs carried no guard load. These volumes are unchanged: rod_ring 218.1941, saddle_and_stem 485.8098, left_guard 77.5911, right side 56.009. Full-rod overlap is 0. r67-saddle.png against front-0.png shows the three diagonal strips gone. A separate 0.497 mm3 free piece in the search box, also present in R66, is unidentified; its gate is < 0.6.

Lead-in and fixed seat (op1-route.json lead_in block). The lead-in removes 1.427 mm3 with max z 7.97, below the 9.4 seat. Seat support at z 8.8, 9.05 and 9.3 is identical to R66; at z9.05: whole 177.64, left 100.79, right 94.7, plunger 2.47. The three holes keep clear radius 1.739 at z 9.05, 8.3 and 7.6, with unchanged 1 mm-ring plastic at 7.6 (0.734/0.97/0.966). Stops are identical. Deposited evidence: printed-seat.json passes in both archives with whole 158.39, plunger 2.41, rings 0.711/0.946/0.939 and the known-bad R64 rejected. op1-independent-section.json at z9.3 gives bore clear radii 1.647/1.649/1.666 with bearing in 76/90/90 of 90 directions. The right guard roots are deliberately excluded from the chamfer by a 0.3 mm keep.

Route matches the requested intent. Unplug the white plug, tip it with the lead hanging down, and raise it from below beside the rod, inside the right guard and through the opening. Mate it above the holder, lower the bare board onto the three holes, then press the lead into the channel. op1-route.json not_feasible reports that pushing the plug up into an already-seated board overlaps the rod (1.01 mm3) and the carrier (12.82 mm3). It also reports that a pre-mated board cannot pass the closed deck ring at z 7.7-9.2. Thread gaps: through_deck 0.75, below_and_above_deck 0.784, full_rod 2.135, to_carrier 0. Drop overlap is 0 for all actors, and housing plus plug with a 0.2 mm gap is 0. In fit.json for each archive, op1_plug_threads_up_from_below (4702 nearby samples), op1_lead_while_plug_turns (4439) and every op1_*_lowered_onto_seat route are unobstructed. The backer positive controls are still obstructed. assembly-guide.json binds carrier a83ac4df and route report cf607c69.

Is the hole big enough? Not proven for the real plug. The passing sweep is for a photo-estimated 3.1 x 6.2 x 3.65 mm envelope at the modelled 10-degree pose. approach_below_deck is descriptive only: it is gated just > 0 and ignores orientation. Its narrowest free radius is 3.16 at z4, and over z -4..7 it ranges 3.16-5.3. That is below the envelope's half-diagonal, so the plug passes only near the modelled orientation. No plug-size limit should be inferred from it. The lead-in guides only at the deck's own underside edge; members below the deck are not chamfered.

Kit is complete: 13 parts, including Hinge_Pin, Hinge_Pin_Snug, Pin_Clip, Pin_Clip_Spare and DFR_Clip_Left/Right. Minimum separation is 3.399 and the machine check passed. Rod: min clear 8.297, no layers under 8, min radius 4.148. Hinge_Pin clearance is 0.192 and pin-fit passes (0.2001). click-fit.json is bound to a83ac4df: contact 0.0032 deg < case stop 1.259 deg, travel 0.8216.

Report labelling. In battery.json, spring_root.volume_r66_mm3 = 41.687 is really the R67 value (it equals diagonal_corner.root_post_mm3.r67). The shoe_preload 'r66' key and the top-level 'r66' blocks in op1-route.json carry the same inherited labels. Cite the diagonal_corner and lead_in blocks instead. fin-design.json removal text still says four fins underneath and two on top, but the file lists three -y and three +y fins.
inadequate_proof: The op1_plug_turns_above_holder scan is vacuous (0 nearby samples), so that motion has CAD evidence only.
Plug and housing dimensions are photo estimates; no dimensioned drawing exists.
Deposited seat and bore evidence covers only z 8.8-9.3. Near the socket holes, the 7.25-7.97 lead-in band is checked only by CAD (three_holes at z7.6 unchanged) plus the layer-164 run.
I made no independent bead probes: Python, diff and cmp were unavailable. I compared the reopened archive by grep of key fields and did not open the G-code this round.
No one has shown that the current design67.py regenerates the carrier at hash a83ac4df after the 16:11 edit.
The bed-end post width and the -y fin's overhang past the diagonal are my hand calculations, not report fields.
residual_unknowns: Real plug threading from below: orientation, tool access in the ~11 mm channel (z -4..7), lead stiffness, and whether the lead-in actually catches the plug.
Board seating with the real housing and plug, whether the keeper holds, and whether clicks repeat.
Pouch insertion, retention and removal, including the outboard lip ending at Y 34.
Cutting the -y tie under the narrowed bed end of the root post without nicking it, and peeling the base sheet.
PETG strings or blobs in the opening and lead-in, sag of the layer-164 bridge, socket teardrops and the rod bore.
Collet grip on the real carbon tube.
physical_checks: Watch the first ~3.6 mm of print height (diagonal corner and moved ties) and the outboard lip start at ~9.8 mm (layer 49).
After printing, cut the -y tie (X -22.4) and the +y tie (X -22.0) flush. Inspect the post end and confirm the spring leaf flexes freely.
Compare the real white plug and housing with the modelled 3.1 x 6.2 x 3.65 envelope before threading.
With the rod and guards installed, thread the plug from below as the guide shows. Then mate it above, seat the board on the three holes, slide the keeper in and check repeated clicks.
Test pouch insertion, retention and removal, and collet grip. Use the standard pin and the clip; keep the spare.
